problem_complexity.detailed_justification:
1 stable, chronic illness: Chronic kidney disease. 3 chronic illness with exacerbation, progression, or side effects of treatment: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia (not at goal), Left knee osteoarthritis with worsening pain, Hypertension (above goal).
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia (not at goal): A&P documents poor control and active management: "A1c elevated at 8.9%; home glucose readings 180 to 240 mg/dL" with medication management plan "Continue insulin glargine 28 units nightly" and adherence intervention "Reviewed adherence strategies for missed evening insulin doses." Not-at-goal diabetes being actively managed meets chronic illness with exacerbation/poor control (Moderate).
Chronic kidney disease: A&P addresses ongoing CKD management/monitoring: "Continue renal monitoring. Avoid NSAIDs. Consider nephrology referral if renal function worsens." No documentation of acute worsening or complications requiring escalation today, so chronic and treated as stable for problem-type classification.
Left knee osteoarthritis with worsening pain: A&P explicitly states worsening symptoms and provides active treatment: "Left knee osteoarthritis with worsening pain" and corticosteroid injection performed; worsening symptomatic OA qualifies as chronic illness with exacerbation (Moderate).
Hypertension (above goal): A&P documents not-at-goal status and ongoing management: "BP above goal today at 148/86. Continue lisinopril. Home BP log requested." Hypertension above goal being actively managed meets chronic illness with poor control (Moderate).

em.pc_critic_response: The prior assessment’s overall level (Moderate) is supportable, but it understated the drivers: diabetes and hypertension are not at goal (poor control), and knee OA is explicitly documented as worsening; each independently meets Moderate (chronic illness with exacerbation/poor control). CKD is also addressed but without documented worsening, so it remains stable chronic. Under the core rule, overall Problem Complexity is Moderate because at least one addressed problem meets the Moderate category (in fact, multiple do). Assumption: CKD treated as stable because A&P lacks explicit worsening/escalation today.
em.dc_critic_response: 1) DISC: Reviewed A&P for explicit 'discussed with' another clinician (names/addresses). Only a conditional nephrology referral is mentioned, which is not a management discussion; therefore DISC not present. 2) Intpr: Checked for radiology tests (X-ray/CT/MRI) with physician independent interpretation language. Only 'prior imaging showed degenerative joint disease' is referenced without any independent read or current radiology report; therefore Intpr not present. 3) IHx: Confirmed history is provided by the patient with no third-party historian statements; patient is capable of giving history; therefore IHx not present. 4) Tests & Documents count: Count only unique tests/documents ordered/reviewed during this encounter. The EHR shows one non-medication order (CBC) which counts as 1 ordered test. Prior week labs (A1c, eGFR/creatinine, urine albumin/creatinine) are described as outside this visit and not explicitly documented as reviewed as results by the clinician for data credit; planned repeat labs in 3 months are future/conditional and not ordered here; therefore they are not counted.
